data.name: Cyprus
data.summary: No tax on gains from shares and bonds (listed or not, domestic or foreign) for any resident; capital gains tax (20%) applies only to Cyprus real estate and shares of companies holding it. No inheritance, estate or gift tax since 2000 and no wealth tax. Dividends: a newcomer without a Cyprus domicile of origin is 'non-dom' for 17 of 20 years and pays no Special Defence Contribution (SDC); only the 2.65% health contribution (GHS, capped at EUR 180,000 of income) applies. After 17 years SDC on dividends is 5% (2026 reform, down from 17%), usually fully offset by foreign withholding tax; non-dom status can be bought for two further 5-year blocks at EUR 250,000 each.

regimes.name: Tax resident, Cyprus-domiciled for SDC
regimes.description: Ordinary Cyprus tax residence for an individual who is domiciled in Cyprus for Special Defence Contribution (SDC) purposes: a Cypriot by domicile of origin, or a foreigner after 17 of the last 20 years of residence (unless the lump-sum extension is bought). A newly arriving foreign family is NOT in this regime for its first 17 years; see the non_dom regime.
regimes.eligibility: Cyprus tax residence (183-day rule, or 60-day rule with Cyprus business/employment/directorship and a permanent home in Cyprus) plus Cyprus domicile for SDC (domicile of origin, or deemed domicile after 17 of 20 years of residence).

capital_gains.summary: Gains on 'titles' (shares, bonds, options, fund units), listed or unlisted, Cypriot or foreign, are unconditionally exempt from income tax. Capital gains tax (CGT) of 20% applies only to Cyprus immovable property and to shares of companies holding Cyprus property (directly, or indirectly where from 2026 at least 20% of their value derives from it; listed shares excluded). Foreign real estate gains are not taxed in Cyprus.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: From 1 Jan 2026, lifetime CGT exemptions: EUR 150,000 for a principal private residence (conditions), EUR 50,000 farmland of a farmer, EUR 30,000 any other disposal, overall cap EUR 150,000 (before 2026: EUR 85,430 / 25,629 / 17,086). Gifts to children, spouse and relatives up to third degree, to family companies and charities are exempt from CGT (conditions).
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Applies to all Cyprus tax residents regardless of domicile.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Property transfer levy of 0.4% of sale proceeds on Cyprus property (and shares of property-holding companies; listed shares exempt), paid by seller. From 2026 crypto-asset gains are taxed at a flat 8%. From 2031, redemptions of units/shares in certain corporate collective investment schemes are treated as dividends.

open_questions: Statute text (Income Tax Law art. 8 exemption for titles; Capital Gains Tax Law as amended Dec 2025) not opened; figures from PwC and Trident Trust.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Securities gains exempt from income tax and outside CGT; private_business_sale = 0 assumes the company does not derive 20%+ of its value from Cyprus immovable property (otherwise 20% CGT on the property-attributable gain). Real estate local = 20% CGT on the gain (plus 0.4% levy on proceeds, not included).
capital_gains.professional_trader: The 'titles' exemption applies even to trading gains (gains on titles are excluded from income tax regardless of frequency), so there is no professional-trader recharacterisation risk for securities. Profits from trading in real estate are business income taxed at income tax rates up to 35%.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign securities and foreign real estate gains are not taxed in Cyprus.

dividends.summary: Dividends are exempt from personal income tax. A resident domiciled individual pays SDC: 5% on dividends paid out of profits of 2026 onwards (17% for profits of tax years up to 2025, grandfathered when distributed by end-2031). GHS health contribution of 2.65% also applies to dividend income, capped at EUR 180,000 of total annual income (maximum about EUR 4,770). Foreign withholding tax is credited against SDC, so a typical 15% treaty WHT eliminates the 5% SDC.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: GHS cap EUR 180,000 of annual income.
dividends.important_exceptions: Dividends from Cyprus companies paid out of pre-2026 profits keep 17% SDC. The 2026 reform abolished deemed dividend distribution but widened the dividend definition (capital reductions, liquidations, redemptions, certain capitalisations) and introduced disguised dividend rules.

open_questions: Official SDC Law text as amended (Dec 2025) not opened.
dividends.rate_basis: SDC 5% on post-2025 profits; GHS 2.65% excluded from the rate because it is capped at EUR 180,000 of income (immaterial for a large portfolio).
dividends.withholding_outbound: Generally 0% on dividends paid to non-resident individuals and companies. Exceptions: 17% on dividends from non-listed companies to companies in EU-blacklisted jurisdictions; from 2026 a WHT on dividends to related companies in low-tax jurisdictions (PwC states both 5% and 17%; unresolved).
dividends.treaty_network: About 67 double tax treaties (PwC table), including the US (1984 treaty) and nearly all EU states; unilateral credit relief also available.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Corporate tax 15% from 2026; dividends received by a Cyprus company are generally exempt.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no recurring levy on financial assets. The annual immovable property tax was abolished from 1 January 2017.

sources.title: Cyprus - Individual - Other taxes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: National immovable property tax abolished 2017. Municipalities charge small local fees (refuse, sewerage, municipal property fee) based on property value.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. Estate duty was abolished from 1 January 2000. Lifetime gifts to children are free of CGT (even of Cyprus property) and Land Registry transfer fees on a free transfer of property from parent to child are nil. Stamp duty was fully repealed from 1 January 2026.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: No thresholds needed: no tax applies.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Executor must file a statement of the deceased's assets and liabilities with the Tax Department within 6 months of death. Probate/court and legal fees apply in practice.

open_questions: Estate Duty abolition law (reported as Law 118(I)/2000) not opened on CyLaw; abolition confirmed by PwC Cyprus.
inheritance.gift_tax: None. Gifts to children are also exempt from CGT and from property transfer fees.
inheritance.foreign_assets: No tax on any assets, Cypriot or foreign.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Not relevant (no tax). Succession law (forced heirship) may apply to Cyprus-domiciled persons; EU Succession Regulation allows choice of nationality law.

regimes.name: Non-domiciled resident (SDC exemption, 17 years, extendable)
regimes.description: Automatic for a new resident without a Cyprus domicile of origin: exempt from SDC on dividends and interest until resident 17 of the last 20 years. From 1 Jan 2026 (Art. 3D SDC Law) a deemed-domiciled person can extend non-dom status for up to two further 5-year periods by paying EUR 250,000 upfront per period (irrevocable, non-refundable, Commissioner approval; Circular 2/2026). Capital gains, inheritance and wealth treatment are the same as standard.
regimes.eligibility: Cyprus tax residence; no Cyprus domicile of origin (normally the father's domicile at birth). No application needed. Extension: individuals deemed domiciled under Art. 2(3) SDC Law; apply by 30 June of the first year of the 5-year period (transitional deadline 30 June 2026 for those deemed domiciled in 2024-2026).

dividends.summary: Non-doms pay no SDC on dividends (domestic or foreign), so no Cyprus income tax or SDC applies. The GHS health contribution of 2.65% still applies to dividend income up to the EUR 180,000 income cap (max about EUR 4,770 per person per year). Foreign withholding tax is a final cost.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: GHS cap EUR 180,000 of annual income.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: Non-domiciled for SDC: for 17 of 20 years of residence; extendable 2 x 5 years at EUR 250,000 per period (total EUR 500,000 for 10 more years).
dividends.important_exceptions: Anti-abuse provisions apply. Non-doms married to a Cypriot domiciliary are still assessed on their own domicile.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if more than 183 days in Cyprus in the calendar year, or under the 60-day rule: at least 60 days in Cyprus, not in any other single state for more than 183 days, business/employment/directorship of a Cyprus company held at year end, and a permanent home in Cyprus (owned or rented) all year. From 1 Jan 2026 the condition 'not tax resident in any other state' was removed from the 60-day rule.

routes.name: Permanent residence by investment (immigration permit)
routes.requirements: Investment of at least EUR 300,000 excl. VAT in new residential property (up to two units), commercial property, shares of a Cyprus company with presence and 5 employees, or Cyprus fund units. Secured annual income EUR 50,000 plus EUR 15,000 for the spouse and EUR 10,000 per child (income must be foreign for the residential route). Covers spouse and minor children; dependent children 18-25 in education apply separately. Visit at least once every 2 years.

Deemed dividend distribution abolished for profits from 2026. Losses carried forward 7 years. Pillar Two 15% top-up for large groups. Cyprus IP box available.

income.name: Cyprus

income_tax.summary: From 1 January 2026 resident income tax is 0% to EUR 22,000, 20% to 32,000, 25% to 42,000, 30% to 72,000 and 35% above. Employees pay 8.8% social insurance up to EUR 68,904 and 2.65% GHS (health) up to EUR 180,000; the self-employed pay 16.6% and 4.0%. The recorded combined rates are 11.45% and 20.6% with the social-insurance cap.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Social insurance 16.6% (since 2024) plus GHS 4.00% of income (PwC other taxes, opened 2026-10-15). PwC says self-employed contributions are subject to a minimum and a maximum that depend on profession or trade, set annually, but lists no figures; the cap recorded (EUR 68,904) is the 2026 EMPLOYEE ceiling applied by assumption and could not be confirmed (Ministry of Labour pages returned 404). GHS applies to income up to EUR 180,000, so above EUR 68,904 the recorded rates overstate by the GHS part (2.65% employees, 4% self-employed). Business profits are taxed on the normal scale after deductible expenses.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. The 0% bracket to EUR 22,000 stands in for the tax-free amount. Dividends and interest face Special Defence Contribution only for domiciled residents (domicile after 17 of the last 20 years).

open_questions: Self-employed maximum insurable earnings for 2026 not found on any official page; the employee ceiling of EUR 68,904 (confirmed for employees on PwC) is assumed. Confidence low for the self-employed cap.

Social insurance and GHS deductions share an overall cap of 1/5 of chargeable income with life insurance, pension/provident (10% of remuneration) and medical fund (2%) items; at EUR 54,000 the cap (EUR 10,800) exceeds the recorded employee contributions (11.45% = about EUR 6,183), so 1 is used. No standard employment deduction on the page.

regimes.name: Digital nomad visa
regimes.description: Visa for non-EU remote workers with stable income of at least EUR 3,500 a month NET (after taxes and contributions) per Remote Work Europe, valid one year and renewable for up to two further years (three in total), capped at 500 permits. min_income is a gross equivalent: EUR 42,000 net needs about EUR 61,000 gross for a self-employed person (16.6% + 4% contributions) and about EUR 54,700 for an employee, using the 2026 Cyprus scale (our arithmetic). The visa does not change tax: a resident (over 183 days) pays the normal scale on worldwide income, and the non-dom regime exempts dividends and certain interest from Special Defence Contribution. The 100% exemption for remuneration for work exercised OUTSIDE Cyprus for over 90 days a year for a non-resident employer (PwC) does not cover work done in Cyprus.
regimes.duration_note: One year plus two one-year renewals.

open_questions: Official page (gov.cy / Migration Department) returned 403; threshold, net basis, duration and the 500-permit cap rest on Remote Work Europe only.

regimes.name: 50% exemption on first employment in Cyprus
regimes.description: Half of employment income is exempt for 17 years for people whose first employment in Cyprus starts after 1 January 2022, who were not Cyprus tax resident for at least 15 consecutive years before, and whose remuneration exceeds EUR 55,000 a year. Usable once per person; not combinable with the 20% or 25% exemptions.

regimes.name: 20% exemption on first employment in Cyprus
regimes.description: 20% of employment income is exempt, capped at EUR 8,550 a year, for seven years starting the tax year after employment begins. Requires employment starting after 26 July 2022, at least three consecutive non-resident years and prior employment abroad by a non-resident employer. Not combinable with the 50% or 25% exemptions.

regimes.name: 25% exemption on first employment or business in Cyprus (2025-2030 starters)
regimes.description: PwC (income determination): 25% of employment income or business profits earned in Cyprus is exempt, up to EUR 25,000 a year, for seven years, for employment or a business starting between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2030. Conditions: Cyprus tax resident; remuneration or profits above EUR 30,000 in the 12 months after commencement; non-resident for the seven preceding tax years; a recognised university degree plus 36 months of full-time non-Cyprus employment in the prior 84 months (or 84 months). Not combinable with the 50% or 20% exemptions. The EUR 25,000 cap on the exempt amount is not representable: it binds above EUR 100,000 of income, where exempt_share overstates the relief.
regimes.duration_note: Seven years; applies to employment or business starting between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2030.
